summary.title: Blow-up and global existence for a general class of nonlocal nonlinear coupled wave equations
summary.authors: N. Duruk, H. A. Erbay, A. Erkip
summary.executive_summary: This paper investigates the initial-value problem for a general class of nonlinear nonlocal coupled wave equations defined on the real line. The model involves convolution operators with kernel functions whose Fourier transforms are nonnegative and satisfy specific decay estimates. The authors demonstrate that this general framework encompasses well-known physical models, including coupled Boussinesq-type equations arising in elasticity and quasi-continuum approximations of dense lattices. The primary contributions of the study are the establishment of local existence theory for solutions in Sobolev spaces, the derivation of a conservation law for energy, and the proof of sufficient conditions for both finite-time blow-up and global existence of solutions. The local existence result holds for kernels with smoothness parameters r_i >= 2 and initial data in H^s for s > 1/2. The energy identity is derived under the assumption that the nonlinear terms satisfy an exactness condition, allowing the definition of a conserved energy functional. For finite-time blow-up, the authors utilize a convexity argument (Lemma 4.1) to show that if the initial energy is negative and the nonlinear potential satisfies a specific growth condition relative to the energy, the solution norm becomes unbounded in finite time. Conversely, global existence is proven for two distinct classes of kernels: first, for sufficiently smooth kernels where r_i > 3, provided the nonlinear potential is bounded from below by a quadratic term; and second, for mildly singular kernels (such as the exponential kernel 1/2 e^{-|x|}) where the Fourier transform decays like (1+xi^2)^{-1}, provided the nonlinear terms satisfy a specific integrability condition. The results resolve open problems regarding the global well-posedness and blow-up for coupled higher-order Boussinesq systems by treating them as special cases of the more general nonlocal model. The paper bridges the gap between abstract nonlocal elasticity models and specific dispersive wave equations, providing rigorous mathematical foundations for understanding wave propagation in nonlocal media.

Executive Summary
This paper investigates the initial-value problem for a general class of nonlinear nonlocal coupled wave equations defined on the real line. The model involves convolution operators with kernel functions whose Fourier transforms are nonnegative and satisfy specific decay estimates. The authors demonstrate that this general framework encompasses well-known physical models, including coupled Boussinesq-type equations arising in elasticity and quasi-continuum approximations of dense lattices. The primary contributions of the study are the establishment of local existence theory for solutions in Sobolev spaces, the derivation of a conservation law for energy, and the proof of sufficient conditions for both finite-time blow-up and global existence of solutions. The local existence result holds for kernels with smoothness parameters r_i >= 2 and initial data in H^s for s > 1/2. The energy identity is derived under the assumption that the nonlinear terms satisfy an exactness condition, allowing the definition of a conserved energy functional. For finite-time blow-up, the authors utilize a convexity argument (Lemma 4.1) to show that if the initial energy is negative and the nonlinear potential satisfies a specific growth condition relative to the energy, the solution norm becomes unbounded in finite time. Conversely, global existence is proven for two distinct classes of kernels: first, for sufficiently smooth kernels where r_i > 3, provided the nonlinear potential is bounded from below by a quadratic term; and second, for mildly singular kernels (such as the exponential kernel 1/2 e^{-|x|}) where the Fourier transform decays like (1+xi^2)^{-1}, provided the nonlinear terms satisfy a specific integrability condition. The results resolve open problems regarding the global well-posedness and blow-up for coupled higher-order Boussinesq systems by treating them as special cases of the more general nonlocal model. The paper bridges the gap between abstract nonlocal elasticity models and specific dispersive wave equations, providing rigorous mathematical foundations for understanding wave propagation in nonlocal media.

Research Context
The study focuses on a general class of nonlinear nonlocal coupled wave equations. The model involves convolution operators with kernel functions having nonnegative Fourier transforms. Well-known examples include coupled Boussinesq-type equations from elasticity and lattice approximations. The system generalizes single equations arising in one-dimensional nonlocal elasticity. Previous studies addressed the Cauchy problem for specific coupled Boussinesq systems. Global well-posedness for coupled higher-order Boussinesq systems was an open problem. This article resolves these problems by considering a more general problem.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question is the existence and behavior of solutions to the nonlocal Cauchy problem. The authors hypothesize that local existence holds for general kernels with r_i >= 2. They predict finite-time blow-up under conditions of negative initial energy and specific nonlinear growth. They hypothesize global existence for sufficiently smooth kernels with r_i > 3. They also hypothesize global existence for mildly singular kernels like the exponential kernel. The exactness condition is hypothesized necessary for the conservation law. The predicted outcome is a unified framework for analyzing various dispersive wave models.

Methodological Details
The study analyzes the initial-value problem for two coupled equations u1 and u2. The nonlinear functions g1 and g2 must satisfy an exactness condition. This condition implies the existence of a potential function G(u1, u2). The kernel functions beta_i are assumed to be integrable. The Fourier transforms of the kernels are bounded by C_i(1+xi^2)^{-r_i/2}. The exponents r1 and r2 are not necessarily integers. The Sobolev space H^s is defined using the Fourier transform representation. The local existence theory is developed for s > 1/2 and r_i >= 2. The proof converts the PDE system into an ODE system in H^s. The right-hand side is shown to be locally Lipschitz on H^s.

Procedures And Architectures
The local existence proof uses standard well-posedness results for ODEs. The operator beta_i * (.)xx is shown to be a bounded linear map on H^s. The energy identity is derived using Parseval's identity. The operator P_i is defined via the inverse Fourier transform. The blow-up proof utilizes a convexity lemma for positive functions. A function Phi(t) is constructed to apply the convexity argument. The global existence for smooth kernels uses Gronwall's lemma. The global existence for singular kernels uses Young's inequality. The singular kernels have a jump in the first derivative. The distributional derivative includes a Dirac measure term.

Key Results
Local existence is established for s > 1/2 and r_i >= 2. The solution is in C^2([0, T], H^s) for initial data in H^s. The energy E(t) is constant in time under the exactness condition. Finite-time blow-up occurs if E(0) < 0 and a specific inequality holds. Blow-up can occur even if E(0) > 0 under certain initial data conditions. Global existence is proven for kernels with r_i > 3. Global existence is proven for mildly singular kernels with r_i = 2. The solution remains bounded in H^s for global existence cases. The results apply to coupled improved and higher-order Boussinesq equations. The model covers quasi-continuum approximations of dense lattices.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The general model unifies various nonlocal wave equations. The exactness condition is crucial for energy conservation. The results resolve open problems for coupled Boussinesq systems. The framework allows for both differential and integro-differential equations. The study provides a rigorous basis for nonlocal elasticity models. The convexity method is effectively applied to prove blow-up. The distinction between smooth and singular kernels is theoretically significant. The work bridges mathematical analysis and physical wave propagation.

Contradictions And Limitations
The local existence result does not require the nonnegativity of the Fourier transform. The local existence result does not require the exactness condition. The global existence for smooth kernels requires r_i > 3. The global existence for singular kernels requires specific integrability of g_i. The blow-up condition requires E(0) < 0 or specific initial data. The analysis is restricted to one-dimensional spatial domains. The kernels must have nonnegative Fourier transforms for the main results. The results depend on the smoothness of the nonlinear functions.

Claims
The general nonlocal model encompasses coupled Boussinesq equations. Choosing specific kernels yields coupled improved Boussinesq equations. Choosing fourth-order kernels yields coupled higher-order Boussinesq systems. The model is more general than just Boussinesq equations. Results apply to known physical wave models.
Finite-time blow-up is possible under negative initial energy. Theorem 4.2 proves blow-up if E(0) < 0. The convexity lemma ensures finite-time singularity. Blow-up can also occur with positive energy under specific conditions. Initial data conditions are critical for solution longevity.
Global existence holds for sufficiently smooth and mildly singular kernels. Theorem 5.1 proves global existence for r_i > 3. Theorem 5.2 proves global existence for mildly singular kernels. Global existence requires specific bounds on the nonlinear potential. Solution behavior depends heavily on kernel smoothness.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The local existence result is robust to kernel sign and exactness. The energy identity relies on the exactness condition. The blow-up proof is sensitive to the initial energy sign. The global existence for smooth kernels uses Gronwall's lemma. The global existence for singular kernels uses Young's inequality.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a unified framework for nonlocal coupled wave equations. 2. The strongest evidence is the proof of blow-up and global existence for specific kernel classes. 3. The future path involves applying these results to higher-dimensional or more complex lattice models.
